purpose: Test parity generalization against independently tuned MSE without selecting on confirmation outcomes
data_rng: default_rng(seed+7), m IID draws with replacement
mask_rng: seed+222; nonzero Bernoulli masks, duplicates retained
selection: Lowest mean negative log likelihood on independent validation draws: 2000 IID draws per development seed, default_rng(seed+50000), shared across all configurations. Select one parity configuration from 20, one MSE configuration from 20, plus the best MSE configuration on the selected parity architecture. Ties break lexicographically. Exact development KL is diagnostic only. Freeze selection before confirmation. Validation adds 20000 development samples; each confirmation model receives only its own 200 training samples.
primary: Selected parity versus globally selected MSE, exact forward KL on 60 new paired datasets. Also require selected parity versus same-architecture selected MSE to support loss attribution. A robust benefit requires both paired two-sided 95% t confidence intervals for parity-minus-MSE strictly below zero. These are intersection requirements, not alternative routes to success.
secondary: Original ring/parity versus ring/raw-MSE at lr=.05; selected sampled parity and selected expected parity versus same-architecture tuned MSE. Secondary tests are exploratory, with 97.5% intervals for the two parity families. Q1000 unseen-elite recovery is descriptive.
budget: Each family has 20 configurations x 10 development datasets x 600 updates. No restarts, early stopping, target-based checkpoint selection, or confirmation retuning. Parameter count and all training/runtime budgets reported. Exact expected parity integrates all masks and is a new simulation extension, not a finite-K hardware reproduction.
claim_boundary: Original 24-parameter IQP and sampled-parity objective preserved. Dense 66-parameter IQP and exact expected kernel are explicit extensions. Confirming an extension is not reproducing a printed paper number. All failures and configurations are retained. No universal or quantum advantage claim.
